101.description: Switching to a terminal WebSocket, started on the machine (a stopped machine is started first). Client to machine: binary frames are keystrokes; a text frame `{"type":"resize","cols":N,"rows":N}` resizes the terminal; `{"type":"stdin","data":"..."}` and any other text frame are typed as input. Machine to client: binary frames are terminal output; a final text frame `{"type":"exit","code":N}` precedes the close. Closing the socket ends the program. The server pings every 30 seconds and ends a session whose client has not answered for 90 seconds; a connection lasts at most one hour, so long sessions should reconnect into a terminal multiplexer.

branched from it, nothing else in the API. Send it as a Bearer token, or as
the `access_token` query parameter on a WebSocket upgrade, so a client that
cannot set headers (a DevTools client, a browser `WebSocket`) can still
connect.

totalMicros.description: Gross subtotal: sum of all resource line items, before discounts/credits.

volumeDiscountMicros.description:

always 0 on per-machine breakdowns).

CreateAgentRequest.description:
Start a managed agent session: a harness (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or
any program) in its own machine, driven as a sequence of turns.

allowHosts.description:
Hosts the agent may reach beyond its model provider and package registry.
The `command` harness has neither, so callers must name hosts or
explicitly opt into unrestricted outbound access.

arch.description:
`amd64` or `arm64`. A session with checkpoints runs on amd64 unless
pinned here.

checkpoints.description:
Checkpoint after every turn so the session can be rewound or branched
(default true).

credential.description:
A stored credential holding the model API key. The session's machine then
never holds the key: the agent sees a placeholder and the node
substitutes the key on requests to the provider, so turns need no key in
their `env`. Its variable must be the one the harness reads (e.g.
`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and its hosts must include the provider's.

model.description: Model: optional for `codex`, required as `provider/model` for `opencode`.

name.description: Session name, unique within the account.

openNetwork.description: Allow all outbound traffic instead of the host allow-list.

program.description: Program for the `command` harness; the prompt is appended.

personId.description:
The account id of the organization member this key acts for. Required when
acting in an organization, and the person the key is narrowed to and
revoked with. A personal account's key is for its owner, so leave it out.

tenantId.description:
Tenant to scope this key to (admin only). Keys created with a tenant_id
can only access resources belonging to that tenant.

mountPath.description:
Absolute guest path machines mount it at unless they say otherwise.
Default `/cache`.

name.description: Unique within your account: 1-63 chars of `[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._-]*[a-z0-9])?`.

sizeGb.description: Size of the cache filesystem in GiB (1-500). Default 20.

ttlSeconds.description:
How long the token lasts, in seconds: 60 to 86400, 3600 when left out.
It never outlives the API key that mints it.

branchable.description:
Create this machine as a branch source: it boots with cloneable live RAM
so `POST /v1/machines/:id/branches` can create independent copy-on-write
children. Default false.

oneOf.description:
A cache disk the machine starts from: a published version of one of your
cache disks, read through the machine's own copy-on-write layer and
mounted at `mountPath`. Branches carry it.

command.description:
Optional workload command (argv) that overrides the source image's or
`.smolmachine` artifact's own entrypoint+cmd when the machine starts, so a
deploy of an off-the-shelf image can say what to run/serve. Empty (default)
= use the source's own entrypoint, preserving prior behavior.

credentials.description:
Names of stored credentials this machine binds. Each gives the guest a
placeholder in the credential's variable; the node substitutes the value
only on HTTPS requests to the credential's hosts, so the machine never
holds it.

labels.description:
Free-form key/value labels for finding the machine again later
(`GET /v1/machines?label=key=value`). At most 32; keys are 1-63 chars of
`[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]*[a-z0-9])?`, values up to 255 chars.

nestedVirt.description:
Expose nested virtualization (VMX/SVM) to the guest so it can run its own
hypervisor. Refused with 422 `nested_virt_unavailable` unless this platform
enables it, so a request for it is never silently dropped. Default false.

ports.description:
Ports to publish (web groups), at most 16. Guest ports only; hostPort is
allocated.

public.description:
Opt in to UNAUTHENTICATED public ingress: when true (and the machine has a
published port), its `*.apps`/`/proxy` URL is reachable by anyone. Default
false — a published port is reachable only via the authenticated path.

remoteMounts.description:
S3-compatible buckets mounted inside the guest. Unlike `mounts` these
place no constraint on which node runs the machine.

CreateOrgRequest.description: `POST /v1/org` creates an organization and makes the caller its owner.

displayName.description: Human readable name, shown in the console.

name.description: The slug: lowercase alphanumeric plus `-`/`_`, 3 to 50 characters, unique and final.

allowAlwaysOn.description: May keep a published-port machine running instead of scaling to zero.

maxDiskGb.description: Largest disk (GB) one machine may request; omitted = platform maximum.

monthlyFeeMicros.description: Flat recurring platform fee (micros per period); 0 = usage-only plan.

durable.description:
Durability of the volume. `false`/absent (the default) is **ephemeral** —
fast node-local storage that is lost if the host node fails. `true` is
**durable** — a disk that re-attaches to a live node on failover (requires
the deployment to have a durable backend configured). This is the
customer-facing knob; it maps to `backend` internally.

CredentialInfo.description: A stored credential, without its value.

publicIngress.description:
Opt-in: expose this group's published port on the UNAUTHENTICATED public
`/proxy` / `*.apps` ingress. Default false — the app is reachable only by
its owner tenant (or admin) until explicitly made public, matching the
per-machine `public_ingress` default.

then destroy old instances.

ErrorResponse.description:
RFC 9457 problem-details error body. Every 4xx/5xx from the API carries
this shape as `application/problem+json`: `code` is stable and
machine-readable (e.g. `not_found`, `too_many_requests`), `detail` is the
human-readable message, and `title`/`status` mirror the HTTP status line.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code for branching without parsing prose.

detail.description: Human-readable description of what failed and how to resolve it.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body for log-friendly errors.

title.description: Canonical reason phrase for the status (e.g. `Not Found`).

type.description: Problem type URI; `about:blank` when the status code says it all.

ForkBatchRequest.description:
Request to branch a running source into many children in one call. The
operation is transactional: if any child fails, every child is rolled back.

branchable.description: Let every child become another branch source.

count.description:
Number of children to branch (1..=`MAX_FORK_BATCH`). Ignored when `names` is
non-empty.

freezeSource.description: Keep the source paused as a reusable branch base, as for a single branch.

labels.description: Labels for every child. Omitted = copy the source's labels.

namePrefix.description:
Prefix for auto-named children when `count` is used. Defaults to the source's
name.

names.description:
Explicit child names. When non-empty, its length is the batch size and
`count` is ignored; otherwise children are auto-named `{name_prefix}-{n}`.

ports.description:
Inbound port forwards applied to every child. Empty means each child gets
fresh host ports so siblings do not collide.

ForkBatchResponse.description: Result of a batch branch: the children, in request order.

ForkRequest.description: Request to branch a running source into an independent copy-on-write child.

branchable.description:
Materialize the child as another checkpoint source so it can execute,
reach a later decision point, and branch again. This pays one eager guest
memory copy while the child boots; its descendants remain copy-on-write.

freezeSource.description:
Keep the source paused as a reusable branch base instead of resuming it.
Later branches restore the same checkpoint, and a frozen source no longer
counts toward the concurrency cap. It cannot execute again; stop it, or
work in its children.

labels.description:
Labels for the child. Omitted = copy the source's labels; supplied
(even empty) = use exactly these.

name.description: Name for the new child machine.

ports.description:
Guest ports the clone publishes. Empty = the source's guest ports. Host
ports are always allocated by the control plane; any `hostPort` is ignored.

InviteMemberRequest.description: Body of `POST /v1/org/members/invite`, declared here so it reaches the client spec.

email.description: The address to invite, matched case-insensitively against the IdP's verified address.

InviteResult.description:
Result of inviting a member: the accept link, which comes back even with no
email provider configured (the admin can copy and share it directly).

emailSent.description: Whether the link was handed to a mailer; false on a deployment with none.

invitationUrl.description: The accept link, carrying the only readable copy of the token.

intoSlot.description: Put in a cache slot by a restore, which needs an engine that serves slots.

slot.description: Attached unmounted, as a slot a restore can put another cache in.

MachineCacheDiskSpec.description: Which cache disk a machine starts from, on create.

cache.description: The cache disk's id or name.

mountPath.description:
Absolute guest path to mount it at; the cache disk's own mount path when
left out.

slot.description:
Attach it as a slot: left unmounted, so a checkpoint of the machine can
be restored with a different cache mounted here (`cacheDisk` on restore).
The slot's size is this cache disk's size; its contents are never read.

version.description: Version to start from; the latest when left out.

MachineCapabilities.description:
Dynamic machine operations for clients that must feature-detect instead of
guessing from a server or engine version.

user.description: Run as this user (image user name or `uid[:gid]`), overriding the image's USER.

background.description:
Run the command detached: spawn it in the background and return its PID
immediately. Use for long-lived daemons (dev server, agent runner).

stream.description:
Stream stdout and stderr as Server-Sent Events instead of buffering the
whole run into one JSON body. The response is then `text/event-stream`,
not `MachineExecResponse`: frames are `event: stdout|stderr|error|exit`
with `data:` lines, and the terminal `exit` frame carries
`{"exitCode": N}`. Streamed output is not capped, so this is the right
path for long-running or high-volume commands.

user.description:
Run as this user: a name from the image or a numeric `uid[:gid]`,
overriding the image's USER. Forwarded to the machine's runtime; an
older runtime that cannot honour it rejects the request rather than
running the command as the wrong account.

stderrB64.description:
Byte-exact stderr (base64), binary-safe and NOT truncated. Serializes as
`stderrB64`.

stdout.description:
Lossy UTF-8 stdout, capped (see `stdout_truncated`). Kept for old clients
and log views; prefer `stdoutB64` for byte-exact, untruncated output.

stdoutB64.description:
Byte-exact stdout (base64), binary-safe and NOT truncated. Preferred by
clients that need fidelity (`smol cloud exec`). `rename_all=camelCase`
serializes this as `stdoutB64`.

user.description:
The user the command was run as, echoed back when the request set one.
A client that asked for a user and does not see it here is talking to a
control plane that predates the field and dropped it — which the
client must treat as an error, never as "ran as the default account".

arch.description:
The machine's actual CPU arch (`arm64`/`amd64`): the arch of the node it
runs on, falling back to `source.arch` (a `.smolmachine`'s pinned arch)
when the machine is unplaced or its node is gone. `None` only when neither
is known. Lets the console show an arch badge for every machine, including
ones whose source pinned no arch. Populated by the server's `machine_info`.

branchGeneration.description: Zero for a root branch source, one for its children, and so on.

oneOf.description: Lifecycle of a live branch source.

branchable.description: Whether this machine can produce live copy-on-write branches.

oneOf.description: The cache disk the machine runs with, if any.

capabilities.description: Operations the control plane can safely offer for this machine right now.

createdBy.description: The account id of whoever created the machine; null when nobody is.

error.description:
When [`Self::state`] is `"error"`, a human-readable reason the machine
failed — the latest control-plane error event (e.g. `"start failed: …"`,
`"auto-start failed: …"`, or `"machine stuck in creating state"`). `null`
for machines that are not in an error state. Gives clients something
actionable instead of a bare `error` with no explanation.

labels.description: Labels set at create time (or inherited from a branch source).

parentMachineId.description:
Immediate live-RAM checkpoint this machine was branched from. `null` for
ordinary machines and root checkpoints.

ports.description: Published ports with their allocated node host ports.

ready.description:
Whether the machine is READY to do work. `state == "started"` only means
the VM process launched on the node — the guest OS and your in-VM workload
still need a moment to boot. `ready` becomes true once the guest agent is
reachable (an `exec`/`connect` will succeed) and, if the machine publishes
a port, that port is accepting connections. Wait for `ready` (poll
`GET /v1/machines/:id`) before expecting an in-guest worker to have started
or before connecting to it — do NOT act on `started` alone.

readyAt.description:
When a probe first observed this machine serving (RFC3339), or `null`.

This is a readiness gate, not a boot timestamp: it is stamped when the
published port accepts a connection (or, for a machine with no published
ports, when its guest agent answers), and it is cleared on every stop so
a restart must re-prove itself. A short-lived machine may finish its
whole life as `null` here without anything being wrong. Use `createdAt`
if you want when the machine came into existence.

rootBranchId.description:
Root source for this live branch lineage. A root points to itself;
ordinary machines have no lineage.

url.description:
Public ingress URL for the machine's first published port, when the
machine is started and the control plane has a public base URL
configured. `null` for stopped machines, machines with no published
port, or when the deployment exposes no public base URL.

MachineLineage.description:
One complete live branch lineage, suitable for rendering as a tree. Parent
relationships remain on each machine so clients do not have to infer them
from names or creation order.

oneOf.description:
No outbound access for the guest. The image PULL runs in-guest too, so a
`blocked` machine whose image isn't already node-cached CANNOT fetch it and
its start fails on an unreachable registry — opt into this deliberately.

Unrestricted outbound access. This is the DEFAULT: it matches what the
`smol` CLI already sends, and means a create that omits `network` (raw
API/SDK) can pull remote images out of the box instead of failing the
start on an unreachable registry. Tighten with `blocked`/`allowCidrs`.

MachinePort.description:
A machine-published port. On create, supply only `port` (the guest port the
workload listens on); the control plane allocates `hostPort` on the chosen
node at first start and routes ingress to it. Publishing a port implies the
virtio-net network backend on the node (TSI is outbound-only).

hostPort.description: Node host port allocated at placement (read-only; ignored on create).

port.description: Guest port the workload listens on.

oneOf.description:
When guest disk writes must reach the node's disk. Unset means `full`.
Branches keep their source's.

arch.description:
Requested CPU arch ("arm64"/"amd64"). Optional: an OCI image is
usually multi-arch (the node pulls its own variant), so `None`
means "no constraint" — but a caller that NEEDS a specific arch
(e.g. x86-only binaries inside) can pin placement with it. Was
previously silently dropped by deserialization.

Canonical CPU arch the packed artifact targets ("arm64"/"amd64").
A `.smolmachine` is single-arch, so this becomes a hard placement
constraint. `None` (older clients) means "no arch constraint".

MachineUsageResponse.description: Per-machine usage + cost for the current billing period ("cost so far").

machineId.description: The machine this usage is for.

MeResponse.description:
Identity self-discovery (`GET /v1/me`): who the caller is and where they
may push registry artifacts. Requires authentication but NO scopes — any
identity may ask who it is. This is how the CLI resolves a bare
`myapp:v1` push reference to `tenants/<tenantId>/myapp:v1`.

registryNamespace.description:
The OCI repository namespace this identity may push to
(`tenants/<tenantId>`), ready to prefix onto a repo name.

subject.description: Acting principal: the JWT subject or the API key id.

tenantId.description:
Canonical tenant id, if the identity is tenant-scoped. `None` for
admin keys and identities without a provisioned tenant.

tenantName.description: Tenant display name (the IdP email/name captured at provisioning).

bootId.description:
Runtime's per-process boot id, forwarded from the node's `/capacity`. A
change between heartbeats means the serve restarted (its warm pool wiped),
which the control uses to prune the node's now-stale pool records. Absent on
an older node/runtime that doesn't report it.

csrPem.description:
PEM-encoded certificate signing request, sent only at registration. When
present, the control plane signs it as the node's mTLS **server** cert
(overriding the CSR's subject/SANs with the validated node id/addresses)
and returns the cert in `RegisterResponse`. The node's private key never
leaves it. Absent ⇒ control plane has no node-CA configured, or this is
an older node; the registration still succeeds (cert fields stay empty).

diskCordonedAt.description:
Set (RFC3339) when the control plane soft-cordons this node for DISK
pressure — its heartbeat-reported host-free disk dropped below the cordon
threshold, so it stops receiving NEW placements. SEPARATE from the
data-plane cordon: the node stays `status = "ready"` and is never reaped;
its running machines are untouched. Cleared when free disk recovers past
the (higher, hysteretic) un-cordon threshold. `None` = not disk-cordoned.

reservedDiskGb.description:
Sum of the (thin/nominal) local-SSD footprints reserved by the machines
placed on this node — the disk-overcommit ledger. Unlike `available_disk_gb`
(overwritten by every heartbeat with the host's live free space), this is a
reserve/release decrement ledger the scheduler gates admission on, so a node
can't be packed past `total_disk_gb * ratio`. Reconciled by the capacity
self-heal. Default 0 (legacy rows / never reserved).

runtime.description:
The runtime this node speaks (e.g. `"smolvm"`). The control plane resolves
a driver from this name; `smolvm_address` is that runtime's endpoint.
Defaults to `"smolvm"` so a node that doesn't report a runtime (the only
runtime today) is handled transparently.

smolvmAddress.description: The runtime endpoint (HTTP address) on this node.

smolvmVersion.description:
The smolvm engine version this node's runtime reports on `/health`,
recorded by the control plane. Read-only: a node never sets it. A
checkpoint is only restored on a node at the capturing engine's version
or newer. Absent until the runtime has been probed.

usedCpus.description:
Real CPU usage as fractional CPUs (e.g., 2.5 = 2.5 CPUs worth of load).
Reported by the node from hypervisor/process stats. Separate from
`available_cpus` (which is allocation-based bookkeeping).

usedDiskGb.description:
Real disk space consumed by VM overlay/storage files in GB. Reported
from filesystem stat of VM disk images. Separate from
`available_disk_gb` (which reflects the entire host filesystem).

usedMemoryMb.description:
Real memory usage in MB. Reported by the node from RSS of VM processes.
Separate from `available_memory_mb` (which is allocation-based bookkeeping).

OrgInvitation.description: One invitation an organization awaits; the token lives only in the invite link.

email.description: The address invited, lowercased the way it is matched at acceptance.

expiresAt.description: When it lapses. After this it is neither listed nor acceptable.

invitedBy.description: The account id of the person who sent it.

role.description: The role the membership row will carry: `owner`, `admin` or `member`.

OrgMachineSummary.description: One machine named in a removal's response.

OrgMember.description: A member of an organization, with their org roles.

name.description: Always null: the roster is read from our own rows, which hold no profile.

picture.description: Always null, for the same reason as `name`.

userId.description: The person's own account id; memberships, roles and removal key on it, not the IdP subject.

OrgMembership.description: One account a person belongs to; the switcher lists these, login lands on the latest.

displayName.description: The human readable name the console shows.

lastUsedAt.description: When the caller last acted here, or null if never; the list orders by it, latest first.

name.description: The slug, unique across the fleet and final once chosen.

role.description: The role the caller holds here: `owner`, `admin` or `member`.

tenantId.description: The organization's tenant id used in `Smol-Tenant` to act in this account.

OrgQuota.description: An organization's limits and usage, counted once across every member's machines.

machines.description: How many machines it has now, by the same count the refusal reports.

running.description: How many are running now, by the concurrency cap's own predicate.

OrgSummary.description: Summary of the caller's org context driving the console's member UI.

canManageMembers.description: True when the caller may invite/change-role/remove members (owner/admin).

displayName.description: The display name the owner may rename; null when the account is not an organization.

isOrganization.description: True when the account is an organization (vs an individual login).

name.description: The slug, unique and final once chosen; null when the account is not an organization.

oneOf.description: How many machines it has and runs; null when the account is not an organization.

tenantId.description: The org's tenant id for `Smol-Tenant`; null when the account is not an organization.

PendingInvitation.description: One invitation waiting on the caller; the address is not carried, it is the caller's own.

expiresAt.description: When it lapses. After this it is neither listed nor acceptable.

id.description: What the accept names, a handle not a credential; the caller's address must still match.

invitedBy.description: The account id of the person who sent it.

organization.description: The organization's display name, falling back to its slug, since the caller has no roster.

role.description: The role the membership row will carry: `owner`, `admin` or `member`.

tenantId.description: The organization it joins, for the `Smol-Tenant` header afterwards.

PlanInfo.description: A reusable plan: quota + per-unit rates (money in integer micros) + budget.

freeCreditMicros.description:
Recurring free credit applied to each billing period, in micros (e.g.
5_000_000 = $5/month free). Discount applies after volume tiers.

maxDiskGb.description: Largest disk (GB) one machine may request; `null` = platform maximum.

monthlyFeeMicros.description: Flat recurring platform fee (micros per period); 0 = usage-only plan.

rateBaseHourMicros.description:
Per-machine-alive-hour "slot" fee in micros (e.g. 40_000 = $0.04/hr). Prices
the held VM slot on top of consumed CPU/RAM — not allocated resources.

selfServe.description:
Whether a tenant may switch itself onto this plan. Operator-only tiers
are false and never appear in the self-serve list.

PortableCheckpointInfo.description: Portable live-state capture; only `available` denotes a completed upload.

downloadUrl.description: Authenticated endpoint that downloads the `.smolcheckpoint` file.

engineVersion.description:
smolvm version of the node that captured it. A restore is only placed
on a node at this version or newer. Absent for older checkpoints, which
restore anywhere.

PublicMachineStats.description:
The lifetime count of machine starts on the platform, served UNAUTHENTICATED
at `GET /v1/status/machines` for the marketing site. Counted from the audit
trail, so it is a real number and only ever grows. Operator-owned accounts
(demos, QA) are left out via the `public_stats.exclude_tenants` server
setting, so the figure means "machines our customers launched".

machinesStarted.description:
Machines started by customers since `since`. `null` when the count could
not be computed — the site hides the figure rather than show a zero.

since.description: The first day the count covers (`YYYY-MM-DD`), when known.

updatedAt.description: When the figure was last computed (RFC 3339).

PublicPricing.description:
The published rate card, served UNAUTHENTICATED at `GET /v1/pricing`. Read
straight from the default plan so the public pricing page and the in-console
billing breakdown share ONE source of truth — no hand-synced copy to drift.
All rates are in micros (1e-6 USD).

baseHourMicros.description:
Base "slot" fee per running machine-hour — the held VM (isolation,
scheduling, readiness), independent of consumed compute.

diskGbHourMicros.description:
Disk GB-hour — both active disk and held storage on a stopped machine
bill at this rate.

freeCreditMicros.description:
Deprecated alias of [`Self::signup_credit_micros`], kept so clients written
against the old contract keep parsing. It once meant a recurring monthly
allowance; that allowance no longer exists, so the value is the same
one-time grant. Read `signup_credit_micros` instead.

signupCreditMicros.description:
One-time credit granted when an account is created, in micros. It is paid
into the account's prepaid balance and drawn down like any other credit —
it does NOT reset monthly and is not a per-period discount.

volumeTiers.description: Graduated volume-discount bands, low bound → high.

PublishCacheDiskResponse.description: The version a publish created, and the cache disk it now belongs to.

RemoteMountSpec.description:
An S3-compatible bucket mounted into the machine.

Deliberately separate from [`MachineMountSpec`], which references a
provisioned cloud volume. The two are opposite kinds of resource: a cloud
volume is stateful, claimed exclusively and pins the machine to its node,
while a bucket is stateless, shareable and reachable from any node. Reusing
the volume type would drag a bucket through claim and node-pinning logic
that works against it.

Credentials come from the machine's `env` (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` /
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, optional `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` and `AWS_REGION`), the
same place every AWS SDK reads them. Without them the bucket is read
anonymously, which is how public datasets are consumed.

RemoveMemberResult.description: What removing somebody from an organization revokes and what it leaves running.

revokedKeyIds.description: The ids of the organization's API keys that were revoked.

runningMachines.description: The organization's machines this person created that are left running.

RenameOrgRequest.description: `PATCH /v1/org` renames the organization; the slug is final so only the name changes.

displayName.description: The new display name, trimmed, 1 to 100 characters, same bound as at creation.

ResizeMachineRequest.description:
Change the size of a running machine. Set any of the fields; each one left
out keeps its current value. RAM and disk only grow; CPUs can also shrink.

diskGb.description: Storage disk size in GiB. Grow only.

memoryMb.description: Total guest RAM in MiB. Grow only.

RestorePortableCheckpointRequest.description: Create a stopped machine from a durable portable checkpoint.

oneOf.description:
For a checkpoint captured with a cache slot: the cache to mount in it.
It must be no larger than the slot's cache disk, and is mounted at the
slot's path unless `mountPath` says otherwise (it must match).

SendAgentTurnRequest.description: Send a prompt to a managed agent session.

env.description:
Environment for this turn only — typically the model API key. Never
stored.

timeoutSeconds.description: Longest the turn may run (default 1800 s).

SetCredentialRequest.description:
Store a credential for credential substitution. The value is write-only:
it is sealed at rest and never returned.

envVar.description:
The environment variable a machine that binds this credential sees —
holding a placeholder, never the value.

hosts.description: The only hosts the value is ever sent to (HTTPS requests only).

SignupAttribution.description:
First-touch marketing attribution, reported once by the console right after a
new account's first login. Every field is optional and untrusted: the control
plane keeps an allowlisted, length-capped, query-stripped copy and ignores the
rest. Stored at most once per tenant and only for recently created tenants.

firstSeenAt.description: When the visitor first landed (RFC 3339), which can precede signup by days.

landingPath.description: The first path on this site the visitor landed on.

referrer.description:
The external page that sent the visitor, as scheme://host/path — the
query string and fragment are dropped before storage.

SignupAttributionResponse.description:
Whether a reported attribution was stored. `false` is not an error: the tenant
already has one, is not a new account, or the report carried nothing usable.

TenantInfo.description:
A tenant (customer account). Quota override fields are `None` when inherited
from the plan. See docs/product-backend-layer.md.

maxDiskGb.description: Per-tenant override of the plan's per-machine disk ceiling (GB).

oneOf.description: How this tenant found us, when it was captured at signup.

TenantMeter.description:
One tenant's metered usage for a period, in the shape a billing system
ingests (`GET /v1/billing/meters`).

diskGbHours.description: Disk gb·hours metered for the period.

egressGb.description: Egress gb (networking, billed by gb total) for the period.

UpdateAutoRechargeRequest.description:
Update opt-in auto-recharge (`POST /v1/billing/auto-recharge`). Omitted
override fields reset to the fleet default (`null`).

amountMicros.description:
Top-up amount in micros (`null` → fleet default). Must be `≥ $1` and
`> threshold`.

enabled.description:
Master switch. Disabling never charges; enabling requires a saved card
(the response returns a `setupUrl` to add one when none is on file yet).

thresholdMicros.description: Trigger threshold in micros (`null` → fleet default). Must be `< amount`.

UpdatePlanRequest.description:
`PATCH /v1/plans/{id}`: change a plan's limits in place. Every field is
optional; only the given ones change. Takes effect on the next machine
create for every tenant on the plan.

UpdateTenantRequest.description: Partial update — only present fields change.

freeCreditMicros.description:
Per-tenant free-credit override (micros). Present → this tenant's monthly
free allotment is set to exactly this, overriding its plan's. Absent →
unchanged (still falls back to the plan). Admin-only.

maxCpus.description:
Per-machine size overrides for this tenant (each `null` = leave as is).
They sit above the plan's ceilings, for a deal that needs bigger machines
without a new plan.

consumedFrom.description:
Start of the period the consumed metrics actually cover.

`totalUptimeSeconds` and `machineCount` are computed over the requested
`from`..`to`. The four consumed dimensions cannot be: they come from the
tenant's running per-billing-period counters — the same numbers billing
charges on — and no per-window consumed history exists to recompute them
from. (Deriving them from the window instead reported PROVISIONED
figures that ran 177x the actual bill.)

So for any window other than the current billing period this differs
from `from`, rather than leaving the response looking as though every
number shared one time base.

consumedTo.description:
End of the period the consumed metrics actually cover. See
`consumedFrom`.

cpuHours.description:
The four metered-and-priced dimensions, over `consumedFrom`..`consumedTo`
— NOT over `from`..`to`. Exec is intentionally absent: it
is metered for the event timeline but priced at $0, so surfacing it as
"usage" here would imply a charge that never happens.

durability.description:
`"ephemeral"` — lives on a single node's disk and is lost if that node
fails (the default); `"durable"` — backed by a detachable disk that
re-attaches to a live node on failover. Derived from the storage backend.

VolumeTier.description:
One band of the graduated (tax-bracket-style) volume discount: only spend
*within* the band is discounted at `discount_bps`.

discountBps.description: Discount applied to spend within this band, in basis points (e.g. 1000 = 10%).

upToMicros.description: Upper bound of this band in micros; `null` = the final, unbounded band.

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys carry scopes; a key with no scopes is rejected. Scopes: `admin` (full access), `machine:create`, `machine:read`, `machine:exec`, `machine:files`, `machine:delete`, `group:write` (legacy alias `app:write`), `usage:read`, `billing:read`, `billing:write`, `members:read`, `members:write`, and `*` (all scopes). Each operation's description states the scope it requires. A user login can act in an organization it belongs to by sending `Smol-Tenant: <account id>`; an API key always acts in the account it was minted for. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code` field; suspended or out-of-credit tenants receive 402; rate-limited requests receive 429 with `RateLimit-*` and `Retry-After` headers.
